definitions.explanation: The government of a shogun in feudal Japan. There were three major shogunates: the Kamakura (1185–1333), Muromachi (1336–1573), and Edo/Tokugawa (1603–1868) shogunates.

examples.japanese: {江戸|えど}{幕府|ばくふ}は{約|やく}260{年|ねん}{続|つづ}いた。
examples.english: The Edo shogunate lasted about 260 years.

examples.japanese: {幕府|ばくふ}が{倒|たお}れて{明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The shogunate fell and the Meiji era began.

examples.japanese: {鎌倉|かまくら}{幕府|ばくふ}は{源頼朝|みなもとのよりとも}によって{開|ひら}かれ、{武士|ぶし}による{政治|せいじ}の{始|はじ}まりとなった。
examples.english: The Kamakura shogunate was established by Minamoto no Yoritomo and marked the beginning of warrior-class government.

notes:
USAGE:
An essential term for understanding Japanese history. The word literally means "tent government" ({幕|まく} = curtain/tent, {府|ふ} = government office), referring to the field headquarters of a military commander. The three major shogunates are:
- {鎌倉|かまくら}{幕府|ばくふ} (Kamakura shogunate, 1185–1333)
- {室町|むろまち}{幕府|ばくふ} (Muromachi shogunate, 1336–1573)
- {江戸|えど}{幕府|ばくふ} / {徳川|とくがわ}{幕府|ばくふ} (Edo/Tokugawa shogunate, 1603–1868)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幕府|ばくふ}を{開|ひら}く: to establish a shogunate
- {幕府|ばくふ}を{倒|たお}す: to overthrow the shogunate
- {幕府|ばくふ}{軍|ぐん}: shogunate forces
- {幕府|ばくふ}の{崩壊|ほうかい}: collapse of the shogunate
